thread:
Carlos M: Hi all 1 - returning from EMEA trip and lost a few taxi receipts. Two rides were in cash (EUR) and one was card (GBP). Total cash ~ EUR 37. Can I still claim them?
Jordan (People Ops): Short answer: yes, but we need stronger documentation for cash fares. Did you get any emailed itinerary or card statement for the card ride?
Carlos M: Yes card ride shows on my statement. For the cash ones I only have a photo of the payment screen the driver used and a photo of the journey on my phone (screenshot of the map) plus two short notes I wrote with dates/amounts.
Finance Bot: Policy excerpt: Missing vendor receipts for ground transport: allowed up to EUR/GBP/USD 75 per item with employee attestation + corroborating evidence (map screenshot, timestamped photo, bank statement showing nearby ATM txn). For amounts above policy thresholds, a vendor receipt is required or claim will be denied. Tips must be itemized; cash tips are reimbursable up to 15% and must be reasonable.
Carlos M: Ok I have a photo of the driver's payment confirmation (no VAT line) and an ATM withdrawal time close to the rides. Does that count as 'corroborating evidence'?
Leigh - Accounting: That should be fine for small amounts. Please create an attestation in the report: "I, Carlos M, confirm I paid EUR 20 on 2026-03-02 and EUR 17 on 2026-03-03 in cash to taxi drivers for business travel (routes listed). Evidence attached: map screenshots, driver payment photo, ATM withdrawal 03/02." Sign with typed name. Also list any tips separately.
Carlos M: I had a small cash tip on one ride, about EUR 3. Should I include that in the attestation?
Jordan (People Ops): Yes, include tip amount in the attestation and mark it as "cash tip". If total taxi + tip per ride > 75EUR we will require vendor receipt. Your amounts are below threshold.
Finance Bot: For VAT reclaim: when vendor receipt lacks VAT breakdown, Finance cannot reclaim VAT. If the taxi company issues an invoice with VAT line upon request, please ask them to email it to accounting@redwood.com and include the original transaction reference. If they don't provide VAT data, the company cannot recover VAT and reimbursement will be gross amount only.
Carlos M: Taxi company said they can email an invoice but processing takes 7-10 days in their system. I already filed travel report; should I wait or submit now?
Leigh - Accounting: Submit now with attestation and tag "missing-taxi-receipt". If the vendor later supplies an invoice with VAT, we will attach and start reclaim. Do not create negative lines; add the taxi payments as one expense line labelled "Ground - taxis (cash)" with separate line items in the comment for each ride.
Carlos M: Great. One more nuance 1 - the card taxi (GBP 14) shows on my card converted to USD by bank at weird rate. Do I put GBP or USD in Expensify?
Finance Bot: Always enter the original currency (GBP) and attach the card statement showing USD conversion. Expensify will convert using their rate; Finance will reconcile using posted bank rate. Add a note with the card exchange rate if you want to help reviewers.
Jordan (People Ops): For completeness: in the attestation list the purpose of each ride (hotel -> client office, etc.) and attach any calendar invites or meeting notes if available. That speeds approval.
Carlos M: Done: uploaded attestation_taxi.pdf, map_screens_03-02.jpg, atm_withdrawal_03-02.png, card_stmt_gbp.png, and meeting_invites.pdf. Tagged the report "taxi-missing-receipts-EMEA".
Finance Bot: Automated check: cash taxi total EUR 37 < policy threshold. Attestation + corroborating evidence present. Tagging for manual review. Expected approval in 2 business days. VAT reclaim pending vendor invoice if provided.
Leigh - Accounting: One more internal note: tips paid in cash should be reimbursed to the employee net; they are not taxable income for the company, but keep receipts attached. We'll route through payroll if any tax reporting is required.
Carlos M: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick guidance 60a
